gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Revopoint MINI 2's headline 0.02 mm is single-frame precision, meaning repeatability. Revopoint rates the same scanner at 0.05 mm single-frame accuracy, so on equal terms it is no more accurate than the 0.05 mm INSPIRE 2.
standout_why: The cited guide (3dprinting.com/3d-scanners/) gives the MINI 2 only as 'Point precision 0.02mm' and the Seal as '0.01mm accuracy'. It mixes local, single-shot and volumetric figures in one list and never says that precision and accuracy differ. The other cited page (3dprinting.com small-format guide) does list both MINI 2 figures (precision 0.02 mm, single-frame accuracy 0.05 mm). Its FAQ defines accuracy, but it never defines precision and never says 'volumetric'. It also ranks on 'resolution rather than headline accuracy'. So rivals carry the raw numbers, but none explains them as repeatability versus accuracy, and none puts the scanners on one basis. The Otter's '@ 60 mm' condition is missing from every rival page I read. The cited guide names the Otter without any figure, and the small-format guide doesn't list it.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's 'MINI 2 = best for small, detailed objects' pick ($929 on its card). On a like-for-like single-frame accuracy basis the MINI 2 is 0.05 mm, the same as the INSPIRE 2's 0.05 mm on our page. Its real edges are the 0.02 mm fused point distance and the 120–250 mm close working range, which are detail resolution, not dimensional accuracy. The Otter's 0.02 mm holds only at 60 mm. For replacement parts that must fit, the table should compare single-frame accuracy, plus volumetric accuracy where the maker states it, and not each maker's best-sounding number.
